_meta.description: Editorial calendar: publishing cadence, seasonal desks and content clusters. Consumed by tools/build.py. The topic queue is carried from data/calendar.json (arena/cd3cddd6-prod2, 2026-11-19); slot 1 shipped early in the 2026-11-19 publication pass (guide-two-baskets-or-one.html).
_meta.evidence_rule: No season or topic is justified by a search-volume or trend figure (D-19 / F-15). Each exists because it answers a question a buyer of the verified five products can actually ask, answerable from the verified register. Seasons follow the US calendar because the marketplace is amazon.com (settings.marketplace).
_meta.last_change: 2026-11-20 (arena/e1dbef32-prod2): three new pages registered — a sourced temperature-chart reference, a leftovers guide and a long read on the two-hour rule — all built from USDA FSIS pages read the same day (S-FSIS-DANGER, S-FSIS-LEFTOVERS) rather than from listing copy. Long reads are now derived from this file by the feed builder, so the feed cannot drift behind the register. published_early records pages that shipped out of queue order. The cadence gate re-measures each long read against the built page (20% slack) so a recorded word count cannot rot.

cadence.rule: Each new guide is added to data registers, to the sitemap and to the RSS feed by the same build. A guide publishes only with its sourced facts and its 'what we could not verify' block. The next topic is chosen from measured queries only after the SG-06 gate (Search Console + hosted endpoint + 14 days of events); until then the queue order is editorial. Publishing a reader page advances next_due_utc in the same commit; tools/checks.py's cadence section fails the build when it does not (F-P35). A slot whose stated source cannot answer its question carries blocked_by and publishes when the source exists, rather than shipping a guess to meet a date.
